reports.title: Ashley Notson
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: the law currently does not require care providers to ensure that carers in a care home have had first aid training
concerns.hazard: lack of mandatory first aid training for care home carers

concerns.quote: all carers carry a mobile or portable telephone so that they can summon assistance if an incident occurs without having to leave the person they are looking after
concerns.hazard: absence of legal requirement for carers to have immediate communication devices

reports.title: Charles Evans: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: None of the Carers employed at Hibiscus House had any training in CPR
concerns.hazard: lack of CPR training among carers

concerns.quote: There was no Registered First Aider at the premises
There was no defibrillator on site
There was no emergency bell/alarm or telephone in the residents' dining room
Post inquest, the Coroner noted the CQC Inspection report for Hibiscus House Domiciliary Care Agency dated July 2019 which rated the facility as 'requiring improvement'
concerns.hazard: inadequate CQC follow-up on improvement plan

reports.title: Michael Waite: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: there is presently no requirement for Support Workers, employed by Peabody to provide 24-hour solo support to clients in supported living accommodation, to undergo certificated First Aid Training including Basic Life Support training, prior to assuming their role
concerns.hazard: lack of certified first aid training for solo support workers

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that care home staff lack required life‑saving training—first aid in the earlier case and CPR in the later case.

links.explanation: Both reports point out that there is no legal requirement for front‑line care staff to have completed formal first‑aid or basic life‑support training before working alone with vulnerable individuals. The earlier report concerns care‑home carers, while the later report concerns solo support workers in supported living accommodation.
links.earlier_quote: The inquest heard that the law currently does not require care providers to ensure that carers in a care home have had first aid training.
links.later_quote: there is presently no requirement for Support Workers, employed by Peabody to provide 24-hour solo support to clients in supported living accommodation, to undergo certificated First Aid Training including Basic Life Support training, prior to assuming their role.
